intro: I'm RedCase's receptionist. I can tell you what the platform does, how it protects your data, and whether a capability is available today or on the roadmap. If I'm not sure, I'd rather not guess.

dual_vault.label: Dual Vault — firm knowledge (Vault A) and Nigerian jurisprudence (Vault B)

vault_search.label: Semantic search across both vaults with page-pinned citations

workbench_analysis.label: Workbench analysis packs: SmartBrief, Summons Response, Contract Review, Red-Teamer

legal_assistant.label: Legal Assistant — one per lawyer, learns in your workbench, your permissions

practice_ops.label: Practice operations: time capture, invoices, conflict checks

deadline_tracker.label: Deadline tracker — shipped, pending counsel validation of computed rules

faq.q: Is my data used to train your models?
faq.a: No. Every AI call is zero-retention — client conversations never touch a model provider's logs, and nothing you write is used to train anyone's model.

Every legal proposition carries a citation to a specific page and paragraph of a stored source you can open and verify. If RedCase can't verify the authority in the vaults, it refuses to answer rather than guess.

faq.q: Who controls access to our firm's documents?
faq.a: Documents are encrypted with AES-256, per-document keys your firm controls. Permission is scoped per user by clearance and explicit grants — a restricted partner brief is invisible to everyone without a named grant.
Vault B indexes jurisprudence from the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, Federal and State High Courts, and the NICN, cited to page and paragraph by ratio decidendi.

faq.q: How does the Legal Assistant learn how I work?
faq.a: One assistant per lawyer, bound to a Workbench. It learns your preferences from the work you do in your workbench — and converses only there, under your permissions, never in shared channels.

positioning: RedCase is an AI-powered operating system for law firms — your knowledge, Nigeria's law, and your operations in one engine, built to optimize your firm's workflow end to end. That's positioning, not a feature claim: everything else I tell you about individual capabilities is exactly what's shipped today or on the roadmap.

workflow.q: How would a 5-lawyer litigation firm use this?
workflow.a: Picture a 5-lawyer litigation firm's day. In the morning each lawyer opens a deadline radar — every court deadline computed from validated rules, waiting for counsel to confirm — alongside overnight intake flags, with any new-client conflict already surfaced before a single engagement letter is drafted. Matter work lives in a matter channel: the team researches both vaults, asks their own Legal Assistant, and battle-cards an opposing brief so nothing is filed blind. Client intake runs a conflict check BEFORE the engagement letter goes out. And billing is captured where the work happens — time is logged in-channel, then turned into a one-click invoice in your letterhead.

workflow.q: We're not technical — is this hard to adopt?
workflow.a: No — you don't need to be technical. RedCase follows the way your firm already works: you talk to it in plain language, upload documents, and work in matter channels. Where do you start? Begin with the Core tier — the whole firm's engine: vaults, channels, research, deadlines, time and invoicing, conflict checks. Then give each licensed lawyer their own Workbench — their personal engine with all analysis packs and the Legal Assistant. You can be live without writing a line of code or changing how your lawyers think about a case.

RedCase is an AI-powered operating system for law firms — your knowledge, Nigeria's law, and your operations in one engine, built to optimize your firm's workflow end to end. In practical terms it replaces the scatter of tools on a firm's desk: the shared-drive file cabinet, the binder of precedents, the spreadsheets that track time and invoices, and the separate research terminals. Those still work, but they don't talk to each other — RedCase brings the knowledge, the law, and the operations together in one place so your team stops re-teaching tools and starts trying cases.

workflow.q: What does my morning look like?
workflow.a: Your morning opens with a deadline radar — every court deadline computed from validated rules, waiting for your confirmation so nothing slips — alongside overnight intake flags. Any new-client conflict is already surfaced before the engagement letter is drafted, so the day starts with a clear picture of what's due and who's safe to take on.

workflow.q: How do I work on a matter in RedCase?
workflow.a: Matter work runs through a matter channel. You research your own knowledge and Nigerian jurisprudence in the two vaults, ask your own Legal Assistant for a grounded read, and when the other side files, you battle-card the opposing brief — procedural and jurisdictional flaws, their probable arguments strength-rated, counter-arguments pinned to binding authority. Every analysis lands in the channel by name, human-reviewable, before you act.

workflow.q: How does new client intake work?
workflow.a: Intake runs a conflict check FIRST — before the engagement letter goes out. The firm's existing clients, matters, and Vault A documents are searched for party-name matches at exact, fuzzy, and phonetic tiers, and any candidate is surfaced for a partner to confirm or dismiss. RedCase won't let you open a new matter and bill the hours on a conflict you didn't see.

Billing is captured where the work happens. Time is logged in-channel — a lawyer drops a time entry while working in the matter channel — and at billing time those entries roll into a one-click invoice in your firm's letterhead. No toggling between a time app and an invoicing tool; the time is already there, tied to the matter.

plain: Your firm's brain. Nigeria's law. One engine. RedCase unites your firm's knowledge and the country's jurisprudence in two secure vaults, and answers with pinpoint citations to real authority. Never invented. Always page-pinned.

Two vaults, one synthesis. Vault A holds every brief, pleading and opinion your firm has written — encrypted, permissioned, searchable by meaning. Vault B holds Nigerian jurisprudence indexed by ratio decidendi, Supreme Court to NICN, cited to page and paragraph.

The engine that refuses to guess. When the authority isn't in the vaults, RedCase says so. Every proposition carries a page-pinned citation you can open and verify. Fabricated citations are a hard failure, tested every release.
A senior strategist on every matter. Upload an opposing brief; get procedural flaws, strength-rated counter-arguments, and binding authority — every section human-reviewable.

Red-Teamer: adversarial intelligence. Cross-examine every brief before the court does. Upload the other side's filing; get procedural and jurisdictional flaws, your opponent's probable arguments strength-rated out of ten, and counter-arguments backed by binding Supreme Court and Court of Appeal authority.

Secure Firm Messenger: your chambers, in your pocket. Matter channels where partners and associates work, with court deadlines, battle cards and analysis results posted into the thread by name. Encrypted under your firm's keys. Your client conversations never pass through Meta.

The OS, not a chatbot: time capture where work happens, invoices in your letterhead, conflict checks before the engagement letter, court deadlines computed from validated rules and pushed to your calendar.
Built for privilege: AES-256 envelope encryption, per-document keys your firm controls, every AI call zero-retention, append-only audit trail, NDPA DPIA filed.

Pricing: Core is everything a firm runs on — vaults, channels, research, deadlines, time and invoicing, conflict checks. Workbench is every lawyer's personal engine — all analysis packs, the Legal Assistant, saved searches. For pricing, talk to us.
